established_findings.statement: Recent literature proposes and prototypes LLM-based systems to translate natural-language intents into low-level network configurations and to automate NetOps workflows.
limitations: Records report prototypes/benchmarks and architectural proposals rather than large-scale production deployments.
Task scope and realism vary across studies (benchmarks, controlled examples).

established_findings.statement: Generate–verify–repair (GVR) or similar architectures that interpose deterministic verification and iterative repair have been proposed and evaluated for improving correctness of LLM-generated artifacts in code and engineering domains.
limitations: Evaluations are largely in code, Simulink, or enterprise software contexts, not specifically on network-configuration verifiers in the supplied records.
Practical effectiveness depends on verifier coverage and repair strategy design.

established_findings.statement: Tool-augmented, agentic LLM systems (LLMs orchestrating external tools/datastores) have been demonstrated to improve domain-specific reliability and enable multi-step automation in several domains.
limitations: Demonstrations are domain-specific (chemistry, drilling, clinical) and do not directly prove equivalent gains in NetOps.
Tool design and domain grounding are major drivers of effectiveness; outcomes do not transfer automatically across domains.

established_findings.statement: LLMs exhibit known failure modes relevant to operational use: hallucination/faithfulness errors, adversarial and prompt-injection vulnerabilities, and poor fine-grained classification in security-sensitive tasks.
limitations: Most vulnerability studies are general-purpose; a subset is domain- or modality-specific (e.g., visual adversarial attacks).
Implications for NetOps depend on workflow design, tooling, and safeguards that vary by implementation.

unresolved_questions.statement: How effectively LLM-based NetOps systems achieve operational semantic correctness (reachability, ACL semantics, routing invariants) when evaluated under deterministic network-verification tools is not established in the supplied records.
limitations: This statement reflects absence of direct evidence within the supplied records, not proof that such evaluations do not exist elsewhere.
Some supplied works perform NetOps benchmarking/prototyping but do not report integration with deterministic network verifiers in a way that demonstrates operational semantic guarantees.

unresolved_questions.statement: Whether generate–verify–repair architectures deliver high practical reliability when applied specifically to network-configuration generation (as opposed to code/Simulink) remains unproven in the supplied literature.
limitations: Existing GVR evidence is from adjacent domains; domain differences (network semantics, verifier expressivity) may materially affect outcomes.
Empirical transferability requires studies integrating network-specific verifiers and fault models.

unresolved_questions.statement: The resilience of LLM-driven NetOps workflows to adversarial inputs or indirect prompt-injection (targeting retrieved/context data) is not evaluated in the NetOps-focused records supplied.
limitations: Prompt-injection and retrieval-based attacks are documented in general studies, but supplied NetOps prototypes do not report dedicated adversarial robustness evaluations.
Absence in supplied records does not rule out unpublished or external evaluations.

candidate_gaps.statement: Among the supplied records there is no published empirical study that demonstrates integrating LLM-generated network configurations with established deterministic network-verification tools (e.g., to close the loop with verifiers) and reports operational semantic-failure rates.
limitations: This is an absence-of-evidence statement constrained to the supplied record set; it does not prove such integrations do not exist outside these records.
Some works propose verification-aware architectures conceptually but do not report full empirical NetOps verifier integrations within the provided materials.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is limited evidence in the supplied records of systematic adversarial-testing or prompt-injection evaluations targeted at LLM-driven NetOps pipelines.
limitations: General adversarial/prompt-injection work exists in supplied records, but NetOps-specific adversarial evaluations are not reported in the NetOps prototypes included here.
This observation may reflect publication timing or scope choices rather than absence of such tests in practice.

candidate_gaps.statement: Public, reproducible benchmarks that measure operational semantic correctness (e.g., reachability, policy compliance) of LLM-generated network configurations under deterministic validators are not evident in the supplied records.
limitations: NetConfEval and related works provide task-focused benchmarks but do not appear to provide standard reproducible suites that combine LLM generation with full deterministic verification metrics in the supplied records.
Absence here is limited to the provided record set.

excluded_claims: LLMs are proven production-ready for fully autonomous NetOps without human oversight (unsupported by supplied records).
Generate–verify–repair architectures have been empirically shown to eliminate all semantic errors in LLM-generated network configurations (unsupported by supplied records).
There is conclusive evidence in the supplied records that adversarial/prompt-injection attacks on LLMs cannot affect NetOps workflows (unsupported).
